name: touch
description: Creates empty files, or updates the access and modification timestamps of existing files.

flags.description: Do not create the file if it does not exist.
Set the timestamp to a specific value, e.g. -t 202501120930.
Use the timestamp of another file as reference.

examples.explanation: Creates an empty file named notes.txt if it does not exist; otherwise updates its timestamps.
Creates several empty files at once — a common way to start a small project.
Updates the timestamp only if the file exists; never creates a new file.
Sets the modification time of report.txt to January 1, 2025, 09:00.

about: Despite its name, touch's primary job in POSIX is updating timestamps; creating empty files is a convenient side effect that made it the standard quick way to create placeholder files.
useCases: Refresh a file's timestamp to trigger rebuild tools such as make.
mistakes: Believing touch edits file content — it never writes data into the file.
